operations.label: Fetch a consumable

equipment.description: The catalogue model to take from the store: a tube, plate, flask, cuvette …

id.description: The id the new container gets

fill.description: { preparation, amount }: fetched ready-filled from the stockroom

operations.description: Take an empty container from the store and put it on the bench. Logistics: whether it costs the learner time depends on the support profile.

operations.label: Transfer a liquid

tool.description: A pipette, burette, volumetric pipette or inoculating loop instance; omitted = poured

technique.description: Technique-quality inputs from the interaction: prewet, immersion, speed, angle

mode.description: Air-displacement pipettes: reverse pipetting (aspirate past the first stop, dispense only to it) keeps viscous or foaming liquids accurate

all.description: Pour out everything that drains (no tool, no volume): the vessel keeps its dead volume and a film on its walls

spot.description: Onto an agar plate: the numbered spot (1-48) the drop stays in, its colonies counted apart (a spot plate)

brim.description: Pour until the destination runs over, leaving no air in it (a BOD bottle or density bottle); give no volume or tool

operations.description: Aspirate from the source and dispense into the destination. Refuses only the physically impossible (volume outside the tool's range, no tip, too little liquid, overflow, a closed container). Delivered volume carries the tool's systematic and random error; a reused tip carries a film of its last liquid. Onto an agar plate, cells stay on the surface; into a gel well, a sample without about 3 % glycerol floats away.

operations.label: Add a solid

mass.description: About how much to take; required unless all is true

all.description: Scrape out everything (from a container); a wet solid carries its liquid, and a filter paper keeps a little

operations.description: Add a solid from a stock bottle or another container with a spatula. The amount actually added differs slightly from the intended mass; weighing tells the learner what they really have. A scoop of a wet solid carries its liquid with it.

operations.label: Lift pieces out with forceps

source.description: The vessel the pieces lie in

destination.description: Where they go: a weighing boat, a tile, another liquid

substance.description: Only pieces of this (by default, every solid piece)

blot.description: Blot them on paper towel first, leaving only a thin film of the liquid

operations.description: Take solid pieces (tissue cylinders or discs, a metal strip, marble chips) out of a liquid with forceps into another vessel. They bring a film of the liquid, much less once blotted, and their heat.

operations.label: Read a volume
operations.description: Read the scale of a graduated vessel at eye level. Burettes read from the top; the reading carries a small parallax error and is rounded to the half-graduation.

operations.label: Read a balance
operations.description: Read the load on the balance pan (minus its tare) as a measurement record, at the balance's readability.

operations.label: Mix
operations.description: Homogenise a container's contents and dissolve soluble solids. Each method mixes a fraction per cycle.

operations.label: Make up to the mark
operations.description: Fill a volumetric container to its calibration mark. The final volume is the nominal volume within the class tolerance (meniscus reading error).

operations.label: Place in

position.description: Position in an instrument with slots (rotor positions 1..n); default the first free one

operations.description: Put a container (or plate) into a place: an incubator, water bath, ice, a balance pan, an instrument. Its temperature then moves towards the place's.

operations.label: Take out
operations.description: Return a container to the bench.

operations.label: Set a device

distance.description: A lamp: its distance from what it lights (light falls as the square of the distance)

filter.description: A lamp: a coloured filter in front of it

humidity.description: The air: relative humidity, 0 to 1 (a plastic bag over a plant raises it to about 0.95)

wind.description: The air: a fan blowing across, low or high

operations.description: Change a device's setpoint (incubator, water bath, heating block).

operations.label: Let time pass
operations.description: Integrate every time-dependent process (temperature, mixing by diffusion, degradation, reactions, colour development) over simulated time.

operations.label: Centrifuge

rcf.description: Relative centrifugal force, e.g. "12000 [RCF]"; or give rpm

rpm.description: Rotor speed in revolutions per minute, converted through the centrifuge's rotor radius (RCF = 1.118e-5 × r(cm) × rpm²)

operations.description: Spin the loaded rotor. An unbalanced rotor stops with an incident and nothing separates; open tubes spill. Sedimentation is T1 (settled solids, clear supernatant). Cells pellet by the centrifugal dose and the square of their size (5 µm algae or yeast at about 1000 × g in minutes; bacteria need several thousand × g for ten minutes); mixing resuspends them.

operations.label: Measure

instrument.description: A spectrophotometer, plate reader, pH meter, microscope, melting-point apparatus, colony counter, UV lamp, gel imager, sequencer, IR spectrometer, dissolved-oxygen meter, mass spectrometer, fluorimeter, voltmeter, conductivity meter, pressure sensor, ruler or hand lens (flies)

wavelength.description: The wavelength read (spectrophotometers) or the excitation wavelength (fluorimeters)

mode.description: Spectrophotometers: one reading, a time course (kinetic), or a spectrum across from-to (scan)

squares.description: Counting chambers: how many large squares to count (default 4)

conditions.description: Mass spectrometers: sprayed from acidic organic solvent (proteins unfold, many charges) or a volatile native buffer (fewer charges)

from.description: Scans and fluorimeter emission: the shortest wavelength

to.description: Scans and fluorimeter emission: the longest wavelength

electrode.description: Voltmeters: the metal the positive (red) lead is on, where the vessel holds more than one

negative.description: Voltmeters: the vessel the negative (black) lead’s electrode is in (the same vessel if left out)

negativeElectrode.description: Voltmeters: the metal the negative lead is on, where its vessel holds more than one

operations.description: Run an instrument on a container, plate or slide. Produces raw measurement records (or, for a microscope, an observation of shapes and colours); nothing is corrected automatically.

operations.label: Calibrate an instrument

buffers.description: Two-point pH calibration: two buffers with labelled pH

operations.description: Set an instrument reference: blank a spectrophotometer against a reference cuvette, or calibrate a pH meter with two buffers (the meter then maps the electrode onto the buffers labelled pH, right or wrong).

position.description: Where on the item: its label area, or (slides) the middle, where the light passes

operations.label: Dispose

container.description: What to empty and throw away (or give an item instead)

item.description: A used tool to throw away: a syringe and needle into the sharps bin

operations.description: Empty a container's contents into a waste stream. Disposal events are kept so that disposal can be assessed.

operations.label: Set a pipette's volume
operations.description: Dial a variable pipette. Refused outside the pipette's range (it cannot be dialled there).

cover.description: The vessel's own cap or stopper, a square of Parafilm (for cuvettes, beakers and tubes without one), or a rubber septum that a needle can pass through

operations.label: Purge with inert gas

container.description: A flask sealed with a septum

balloon.description: A balloon of nitrogen (or argon) on a needle

duration.description: How long the gas flows out through the vent needle

sparge.description: Bubble the gas through the liquid too, taking out its dissolved oxygen

operations.description: Flushes the air out of a septum-sealed flask with an inert gas from a balloon, a vent needle letting it out; the balloon stays on, so the flask stays under the gas as liquid is drawn from it. With sparging, the gas is bubbled through the liquid and takes the dissolved oxygen with it.

operations.label: Flush a syringe with inert gas

source.description: A septum-sealed flask under an inert gas, its balloon on

operations.description: Draws gas from the headspace of a flask kept under nitrogen and pushes it out, three times, so the syringe carries no air into what it is used for. From a flask without a balloon, air comes in behind the gas.

operations.label: Record a value

source.description: The measurement record this value was read from

operations.description: Write a value into the notebook, linked to its source measurement if any.

operations.label: Lay out a plate

groups.description: Items to place: { group, items: [containers], role? }

operations.description: Assign wells to standards, samples, replicates and blanks. The plan is data the later steps follow.

input.description: A measurement record, or values by well

layout.description: The plate layout (which wells are blanks and replicates)

window.description: Initial-rate window from the start of a kinetic read

recordAs.description: Optionally record inputs and outputs atomically in this notebook field

operations.label: Fit a model

z.description: A second independent variable for each point: the inhibitor concentration, for model inhibition

recordAs.description: Optionally record inputs and outputs atomically in this notebook field

sources.description: Displayed measurement references used by the learner

operations.description: A four-parameter logistic (four-pl: y = d + (a − d)/(1 + (x/c)^b)) suits binding assays such as an ELISA, whose response levels off at both ends; samples are read only between 10 and 90 % of its rise. The inhibition model fits rates at several substrate (x) and inhibitor (z) concentrations to the competitive, uncompetitive, non-competitive and mixed mechanisms at once, and keeps the one with the lowest AICc (its fit names the mechanism: inhibition-competitive and so on).

operations.label: Run a statistical test

groups.description: The groups' values (t-tests, ANOVA), or the rows of counts of a contingency table

x.description: One-sample t: the values; regression: the independent variable

mu.description: One-sample t: the mean tested against

expected.description: Chi-square: the expected counts or proportions

operations.description: Outputs the statistic (t, F or chi-square), its degrees of freedom (df, and df2 for ANOVA), the p-value (two-sided for t and the slope), each group's mean, the difference or slope with its 95 % confidence interval, and whether p is below alpha.

points.description: Readings, or group means from average-replicates

recordAs.description: Optionally record inputs and outputs atomically in this notebook field

sources.description: Displayed measurement references used by the learner

report.description: { quantity, sample }: the value is this run's reported result for that sample

recordAs.description: Optionally record inputs and outputs atomically in this notebook field

operations.label: Propagate uncertainty

expression.description: The result, as an expression of the named inputs

uncertainties.description: Each input's standard uncertainty, in its own units (a ±a tolerance is a/√3)

coverage.description: Coverage factor k for the expanded uncertainty U = k·u

operations.description: An uncertainty budget by the law of propagation of uncertainty (first order, independent inputs): the combined standard uncertainty, the expanded uncertainty, and each input's share of the variance, so the dominant source stands out.

operations.label: Dry
operations.description: Dry a container's liquid at the method's rate (air: about 20 µL/min; heat: about 200 µL/min); without a duration, to dryness. Dissolved solutes stay behind as solid, and what exceeds its solubility comes out as the liquid shrinks; cells become a film on the surface. Air-dried cells are only loosely attached and wash off; heat fixes them (and kills them).

operations.label: Flood with a reagent
operations.description: Cover a slide with a reagent (about 0.5 mL) for a time. Stains act on the cells according to the staining model; liquid over unfixed cells lifts some of them off.

operations.label: Rinse with water
operations.description: Rinse a slide or surface with a gentle stream of water: loose liquid goes, and so do most unfixed cells.

operations.label: Flame a loop or spreader

tool.description: An inoculating loop, needle, spreader or forceps

operations.description: Heat a loop to red heat: whatever it carried is destroyed. An unflamed loop carries organisms from one culture to the next.

operations.label: Apply a disc (antibiotic, mutagen or control)

disc.description: A paper disc carrying an antibiotic or a mutagen (or only water, as a control)

position.description: Position 1–6 round the plate (default: the next free one)

operations.description: Presses a disc onto the agar: what it carries starts diffusing outwards at once, while the cells grow. Apply antibiotic discs within about 15 minutes of seeding; a disc put on late leaves a smaller zone. A mutagen acts on the cells as they divide, and kills where it is concentrated.

operations.label: Spot test (catalase, oxidase …)

reagent.description: The test reagent (a drop is used)

target.description: A culture, a slide, or a plate

appearance.description: On a plate: test the colonies that look like this

operations.description: A drop of reagent on cells shows whether they have the trait the test detects (bubbles for catalase, a purple colour for oxidase). A mixture gives a weak, patchy reaction; too few cells give nothing readable.

operations.label: Filter

source.description: Pour everything from this vessel onto the filter first; omitted = drain what is already on it (after a wash)

filter.description: A filter funnel with paper (Büchner or gravity)

operations.description: Solids stay on the filter; the liquid passes into the filtrate except what the wet cake holds (about 1 mL per gram on a Büchner funnel under vacuum, 2 mL per gram by gravity), with whatever is dissolved in it. Liquid on the filter mixes with the cake and reaches solubility equilibrium before it drains.

operations.label: Drain through the tap

funnel.description: A separating funnel (a vessel with a tap), unstoppered

volume.description: Run off this much from the bottom; omitted = the lower layer, the tap closed at the interface

operations.description: Runs liquid out of the bottom of a separating funnel. By default the lower layer goes, the tap closed as the interface reaches it, so a little of that layer stays behind; with a volume, that much leaves from the bottom, through the interface if need be. The stopper must be out for air to get in.

operations.label: Concentrate (rotary evaporator)

flask.description: The round-bottom flask holding the solution

duration.description: How long it turns in the bath under vacuum

operations.description: Turns the flask in a warm bath under reduced pressure. Volatile solvents distil off, a solvent layer taking the water dissolved in it; water standing as its own layer goes only slowly. What does not evaporate is left on the glass: the crude product, with anything that came through the work-up with it.

operations.label: Distil

volume.description: Distillate to collect in this fraction

column.description: A fractionating column between the flask and the still head (none: simple distillation)

operations.description: Boils the pot and collects the condensed vapour: richer in the more volatile component than the pot, and richer still through a fractionating column, up to any azeotrope. The pot is depleted as it goes, so later fractions are poorer and the still head hotter; never distil to dryness.

operations.label: Blot a gel onto a membrane
operations.description: Every lane's protein bands move onto the membrane at the same positions (about an hour in the tank); large proteins transfer less completely.

operations.label: Develop and photograph a blot

membrane.description: A blot lying in a chromogenic substrate

operations.description: Colour builds up where enzyme-labelled antibody is bound: bands where the antibodies found their target, and a background wherever antibody stuck to unblocked membrane. A prestained marker shows on its own.

operations.label: Spot a TLC plate

lane.description: Lane on the origin line, from the left

operations.description: A small volume of solution onto one lane's origin; the solvent evaporates and the solutes stay on the silica. Loading more makes a bigger spot that runs into its neighbours.

operations.label: Develop a TLC plate

chamber.description: A chamber with the eluent in it

front.description: How far the solvent front runs from the origin before the plate is taken out

operations.description: Each compound travels a fraction of the solvent front's distance, its Rf, which falls the more strongly silica holds it and rises with the eluent's strength. If the eluent stands above the origin, the spots dissolve into it instead.

operations.label: Wash wells

target.description: A plate (every well in use) or one well or tube

operations.description: Empty each well, fill it with buffer and empty it again, as many times as asked. What is stuck to the wall (adsorbed protein, bound antibody) stays; what is free is diluted away by the few microlitres a well keeps each time.

operations.label: Collect a fraction from a column

column.description: A size-exclusion or affinity column; liquid on its bed runs in first

buffer.description: The running buffer pushed through the column

into.description: The tube that collects this fraction

operations.description: Each solute leaves the column around its elution volume, which falls with its native size across the matrix's fractionation range: large molecules with the void volume, small ones (salts) with the total bed volume. Bands spread with the column's plate count and with the sample's own volume. On an affinity column, the liquid on the bed (and any buffer asked for; the volume may be 0) passes through: tagged proteins stay until enough competitor (imidazole) frees them, and the rest flows out into the fraction.

operations.label: Run an analytical column (UV monitor)

column.description: An analytical size-exclusion column, equilibrated in running buffer

wavelengths.description: Wavelengths to record (nm), from those the monitor offers; default 280

runVolume.description: How much buffer to run through; default the column volume and 2 mL more

operations.description: Injects a sample on an analytical size-exclusion column and records the absorbance of the eluate against the volume passed: each solute a peak at its elution volume, large ones first, sized by how strongly it absorbs at each wavelength. The sample goes to waste.

operations.label: Spread a plate
operations.description: Spread the cells on an agar plate so that colonies grow apart; unspread cells grow where the drop sat and their colonies run together. The spreader leaves on this plate what it carried from the last one, and takes away a little of this one, until it is sterilised.

operations.label: Streak a sector

sector.description: 1 for the inoculum, then 2, 3, 4 … each drawn out of the one before

cross.description: Whether the stroke crosses the previous sector (a dilution streak); false streaks a separate patch, as when several cultures share a plate

operations.description: Streak one sector of a plate. Sector 1 spreads the inoculum; each later sector drags about 2 % of the previous sector's cells, plus whatever the loop still carries, so flaming the loop between sectors is what leaves single colonies at the end.

operations.label: Pick a colony

destination.description: Broth, or a drop of water on a slide; left out, the cells stay on the loop (to streak or stab with)

appearance.description: Which kind of colony to pick, by its look ("golden")

operations.description: Touch a colony with the loop and put the cells (about 10⁷) into a liquid, or keep a loopful on the loop. From a sector of separate colonies the pick is one strain; from crowded growth (or a slope) it is a mixture.

operations.label: Run a PCR program

threshold.description: Real-time cyclers: the baseline-corrected signal (ΔRn) at which a well's Cq is read

operations.description: Run a program on every tube in the cycler, then hold. Each cycle copies every target whose two primers are present; the efficiency falls if annealing is above the primers' Tm, if extension is too short for the product, or if denaturation is too cool; primers and nucleotides limit the yield; low annealing temperatures make primer-dimers. A real-time cycler also reads every well after each cycle and records its baseline-corrected signal and Cq (Undetermined if it never crosses the threshold).

operations.label: Run a melt curve

cycler.description: A real-time cycler holding the finished reactions

operations.description: Heats every reaction slowly while reading the dye. Each duplex melts at its own temperature, so the negative derivative of the signal (−dF/dT) has a peak per product: one sharp peak for a single amplicon, a lower and broader one for primer-dimers.

operations.label: Run a gel

voltage.description: Volts; negative if the leads are swapped (the DNA runs out of the wells)

operations.description: DNA in each loaded lane runs towards the anode at a speed that falls with the log of its length (range set by the agarose percentage). Bands that run past the end are lost.

operations.label: Set an instrument's controls

objective.description: Microscopes: the objective to turn into the light path (4x, 10x, 40x, 100x-oil …), or none to turn the nosepiece between objectives

illumination.description: Microscopes: the condenser turret, brightfield or a phase annulus (ph1, ph2 …) matching the objective's phase ring

lamp.description: Lamp output as a fraction of full (0 to 1); higher power needs more light

condenser.description: Microscopes: condenser focused on the field, or left as found (uneven light, poorer resolution)

operations.description: Set controls that persist on the instrument. Microscopes: objective, illumination, lamp and condenser. Turning a high-power dry objective over a slide with immersion oil on it takes the lens into the oil.

operations.label: Focus a microscope
operations.description: Coarse focus finds the specimen at low power; at high power (working distance under 1 mm) it drives the slide into the lens and cracks it. Fine focus sharpens an image that is nearly in focus and cannot find one that is not. Objectives are parfocal: after turning the nosepiece the image is nearly in focus.

operations.label: Clean oil off a lens

objective.description: One objective; left out, every objective with oil on it

slide.description: Also wipe the immersion oil off this slide

operations.description: Wipe immersion oil off with lens tissue. Oil left on a dry objective blurs every image through it.

operations.label: Flame the neck of a bottle or tube
operations.description: Pass the open neck through a hot flame, after opening and before closing. An uncovered vessel's rim, handled unflamed, now and then lets a contaminant in (contract contamination).

operations.label: Clean your hands
operations.description: Wash at the sink, or use an antiseptic wipe: fewer skin organisms are left on the fingers.

operations.label: Press fingertips on agar

plate.description: An agar plate with its lid off

operations.description: One gentle press of the fingertips on the agar: the skin flora the hands carry now is left on it.

operations.label: Stab an agar deep

source.description: A broth culture to dip the loop into first; left out, the loop's own load is stabbed

operations.description: Plunge the loaded loop straight down the middle of the agar. Where it grows along the stab shows the organism's oxygen requirement.

operations.label: Search references with a sequence

query.description: A sequence: plain bases or FASTA

operations.description: Compare a sequence with the reference sequences, on both strands (an offline stand-in for a nucleotide BLAST). Outputs the hits ranked by score, each with its title, identity (%), query coverage (%), strand, the span it aligns to and the annotated genes there; `top` and `gene` are the best hit and its first gene.

operations.label: Align two sequences

query.description: A sequence: plain bases or FASTA

subject.description: A second sequence, or the id of a reference sequence

gene.description: The gene whose coding sequence numbers the codons (default: the one the alignment falls in)

operations.description: Align two sequences locally (pairwise, BLASTN scores, both strands). Outputs identity and coverage, and each difference: substitution, insertion or deletion, its position in each sequence, and (against an annotated reference) the codon and its effect: silent, missense (Leu69Pro), nonsense, a frameshift with the residues it changes before a stop, or an in-frame loss or gain.

operations.label: Connect the gas

container.description: The vessel the gas comes from

syringe.description: A gas syringe on a bung: it collects the gas to be read

into.description: Another vessel's liquid for the gas to bubble through (limewater)

operations.description: Fit a bung: to a gas syringe, which collects the gas given off so its volume can be read (from zero now), or to a delivery tube into another liquid, which the gas bubbles through. With neither, the bung comes off and the gas goes to the room.

operations.label: Fit a still head and condenser

flask.description: The flask to distil from (it is heated where it stands)

receiver.description: Where the condensed vapour runs (omit to take the still head off again)

operations.description: Set a flask up for distillation into a receiver: while it boils (at the bubble point of what it holds), the vapour, richer in what boils lower, is condensed into the receiver, so a product that boils below the mixture leaves as it forms. Without a receiver the still head comes off, and the head temperatures and the volume that came over are reported.

operations.label: Test the gas

container.description: The vessel whose gas is tested at its mouth

operations.description: Hold a lighted splint, a glowing splint or damp litmus paper at the mouth of the vessel and see what happens: hydrogen pops, oxygen relights a glowing splint, carbon dioxide puts a flame out, ammonia turns red litmus blue.

operations.label: Flame test

sample.description: The solution or solid the wire is dipped in

wire.description: A nichrome or platinum wire loop

view.description: By eye, through cobalt-blue glass (which hides sodium's yellow), or through a hand spectroscope (the bright lines and their wavelengths)

clean.description: Clean the wire first: dip it in concentrated hydrochloric acid and heat it until it gives no colour

operations.description: Dip the wire in the sample and hold it at the edge of a roaring Bunsen flame: each metal's atoms emit their own light (sodium yellow-orange, potassium lilac, lithium crimson, calcium orange-red, copper green). The colour comes from the emission lines, so a trace of sodium masks potassium, and cobalt-blue glass shows potassium through it. An uncleaned wire shows what it last held.

operations.label: Connect a salt bridge

to.description: The other half-cell; leave out to take the bridge away

operations.description: Lay a strip of filter paper soaked in potassium nitrate solution across two beakers so that it dips into both: ions can then move between the half-cells, completing the circuit without mixing them.

operations.label: Electrolyse

cell.description: The vessel of electrolyte the electrodes dip into

anode.description: The electrode on the positive terminal (an electrode holder with its strip or rod)

cathode.description: The electrode on the negative terminal

current.description: The current set on the supply, e.g. 0.5 A

anodeGas.description: A tube full of the liquid upturned over the anode, to collect its gas (bung it to a gas syringe to measure the volume)

cathodeGas.description: A tube upturned over the cathode, to collect its gas

operations.description: Pass a direct current through the electrolyte between two electrodes for a time. Metal ions or hydrogen are reduced at the cathode; the anode dissolves, or a halogen or oxygen forms there, whichever comes first. Reports the charge passed and what is seen at each electrode.

operations.label: Trap air in a syringe

container.description: A gas syringe that can be sealed

volume.description: The volume of room air to draw in before capping the nozzle

operations.description: Draw a volume of the room’s air into a gas syringe and cap its nozzle, trapping the gas (and any liquid already in it).

operations.label: Hold the plunger

volume.description: Push or pull the plunger to this volume and hold it there; leave out to let it go free (atmospheric pressure)

operations.description: Squeeze or expand the trapped gas to a volume and hold it there, or release the plunger so the gas finds its own volume at atmospheric pressure.

operations.label: Add flies to a vial
operations.description: Tip flies of a stock into a vial: virgin females and males, which mate and leave offspring a generation later if the vial is kept warm.

operations.label: Move flies to another vial

females.description: How many females to move (as virgins)

phenotype.description: Only flies that look like this (e.g. "wild type", "vestigial wings")

operations.description: Etherise flies and move some to a fresh vial as its parents: the offspring if they have emerged (the next generation), otherwise the adults; picked at random, or only those of one phenotype.

operations.label: Set up a side of a choice chamber

humidity.description: Silica gel (dry) or damp paper (humid) under the gauze

operations.description: Set the conditions on one side of a choice chamber: the humidity under its gauze and whether it is covered.

operations.label: Put animals in a choice chamber
operations.description: Put animals in through the centre hole of a choice chamber; they land on either side at random and then wander.

techniques.label: Prepare a dilution series
techniques.description: Prepare a set of concentrations by diluting a stock into separate vessels (each made directly from the stock, so errors do not propagate down the series).

analyte.description: The substance the targets refer to; default: the first component on the stock's label

quality.statement: A fresh tip for every transfer from the stock
Each volume measured with a pipette in its accurate range
Each standard mixed before it is used

errors.statement: Tip reused between the stock and a standard

The tube stays layered (core:mixing/strata); the sample drawn from it is too dilute or too concentrated

support.each: For each standard, work out the stock volume (C₁V₁ = C₂V₂) and add diluent first, then stock, then mix.
support.add-diluent: Add the diluent first, so the stock goes into liquid.
support.add-stock: Use a fresh tip for each stock transfer.
support.mix: Vortex briefly so the standard is uniform before you sample from it.

techniques.label: Serial dilution
techniques.description: Each vessel is made from the previous one, so a constant factor applies down the series (and errors propagate). The last vessel keeps one transfer volume more than the others.

volumeEach.description: Volume left in each vessel after the transfer to the next

quality.statement: A fresh tip for each transfer down the series
Each vessel mixed before transferring from it

errors.statement: A vessel not mixed before transferring on
errors.consequence: The error propagates to every later vessel

groups.description: [{ group, items, role }]: what goes on the plate

quality.statement: A fresh tip for each different standard or sample

techniques.label: Dispense a reagent into wells or tubes
Standard-curve analysis
techniques.description: Subtract the blank, average replicates, fit the standards, and read the unknowns from the fit (corrected for dilution), flagging any outside the calibrated range.

standards.description: The layout group holding the standards

unknowns.description: The layout groups to read from the fit: give each unknown its own group

quality.statement: Every unknown named was found on the plate

stream.description: Default: the definition's declared stream for this material, else its hazard facet

techniques.label: Weigh by difference
techniques.description: Weigh the container of solid, tip a portion into the destination, weigh the container again: the mass delivered is the difference, whatever stays on the spatula or boat.

source.description: The weighing bottle holding the solid

techniques.label: Prepare a burette
techniques.description: Fill the burette with titrant to near the top and read the starting volume.

techniques.label: Titrate to the end point
techniques.description: Without an estimate, add titrant in steps until the indicator changes (a rough titration). With one, add quickly to about 1 mL short, then drop by drop, swirling, until the colour persists.

endColour.description: The colour at the end point (for a precipitate, any of several names separated by |)

watch.description: What changes colour at the end point: the solution (an indicator) or the precipitate (chromate in a Mohr titration)

steps.when: approx != null && !if(watch == "precipitate", mentions(precipitateColour(flask), endColour), colour(flask) == endColour)

techniques.label: Load a centrifuge rotor in balance
techniques.description: Place tubes in opposite pairs. With an odd number, make a balance tube of the same kind, filled with water to the same volume.

by.description: Fill the balance tube with water to the same volume, or to the same mass (for dense solutions)

errors.statement: Tubes not in opposite pairs, or no balance tube for an odd number
errors.consequence: The rotor runs out of balance: vibration, an automatic stop and an incident (core:centrifuge)

techniques.label: Collect a solid by vacuum filtration
techniques.description: Pour the mixture onto a Büchner funnel under suction, then wash the cake with small portions of cold solvent, draining after each.

wash.description: Cold solvent to wash the cake; omitted = no wash

errors.consequence: The mother liquor left in the cake dries onto the product with everything dissolved in it (core:filter)

errors.statement: The cake is washed with warm or large portions of solvent
errors.consequence: The wash dissolves product: the yield falls (solubility model)

techniques.label: Dry a solid product
techniques.description: Scrape the solid onto a watch glass and dry it in a warm oven (or in air, more slowly).

errors.statement: The product is weighed or tested while still wet
errors.consequence: The mass reads high and the melting point is low and broad (core:dry, melting-point model)

equipment.description: A few microlitres infused into an electrospray source in positive or negative ion mode: the peaks (m/z, intensity relative to the base peak). Proteins sprayed from acidic aqueous acetonitrile carry a broad envelope of charges.

equipment.description: Excites a quartz cuvette at one wavelength and scans the emitted light at right angles: an emission spectrum in counts. Too concentrated a sample absorbs its own light (the inner filter effect): keep absorbance at the excitation below about 0.1.

equipment.description: Pumps buffer through a column at 0.5 mL/min from a 500 µL injection loop; a 2 mm flow cell after the column records the absorbance at 280 and 254 nm against the volume passed.

equipment.label: Rotary evaporator
equipment.description: Turns a round-bottom flask in a 40 °C bath under reduced pressure: ethyl acetate, ethanol and the like distil off in minutes, water left as a layer of its own only slowly.

equipment.label: Agar plate (90 mm Petri dish)
equipment.description: A poured agar plate: its preparation is the medium. Liquid put on it soaks in; cells stay on the surface and grow into colonies.

equipment.label: Cell spreader (L-shaped, glass)
equipment.description: Dipped in ethanol and flamed between plates; otherwise it carries cells from one plate to the next.

equipment.label: Forceps (fine-tipped)
equipment.description: For handling discs: dipped in ethanol, the ethanol burnt off in the flame, then cooled a few seconds before use.

equipment.label: Test tube (glass, 16 × 150 mm)
equipment.description: For small-scale tests: a few millilitres of solution and drops of reagent. Hold it to the light to see colours and precipitates.

equipment.label: Boiling tube (glass, 25 × 150 mm)
equipment.description: A wide tube for heating, or for more liquid than a test tube holds.

equipment.label: Gas syringe
equipment.description: A glass syringe whose plunger is pushed out by the gas a reaction gives off.

equipment.label: Flame-test wire (nichrome loop in a handle)
equipment.description: Cleaned by dipping in concentrated hydrochloric acid and heating until it gives the flame no colour; otherwise it shows what it last held.

equipment.label: Gas syringe (100 mL, glass)
equipment.description: Graduated every 1 mL to 100 mL; fitted to a bung in the reaction flask.

equipment.label: Photosynthometer (capillary gas collector)
equipment.description: Gas from a plant in water collects in a flared tube and is drawn into a capillary, where its length is read against a scale: about 0.01 mL resolution, up to 20 mL.

equipment.label: Digital voltmeter (high resistance)
equipment.description: Two leads: red (+) and black (−). It draws almost no current, so it reads the cell’s full potential difference to 1 mV. Across two vessels it needs a salt bridge to complete the circuit.

equipment.label: Conductivity meter (temperature-compensated)
equipment.description: A cell of two electrodes dipped into the liquid: its conductivity in µS/cm (mS/cm above 2000), corrected to 25 °C, and the total dissolved solids it implies (0.64 mg/L per µS/cm). Rinse it with deionised water between samples.

equipment.label: Low-voltage DC power supply with ammeter
equipment.description: Up to 12 V and 3 A, with the current set by a knob and read on its ammeter. Through a poorly conducting liquid it cannot reach the set current.

equipment.label: Glass gas syringe, 100 mL, with a sealed nozzle
equipment.description: Draw in air and cap the nozzle: the trapped gas can be squeezed or warmed, its volume read on the barrel to 0.5 mL, and liquid injected through the cap with a hypodermic syringe. The plunger moves freely (so the gas stays at atmospheric pressure) unless held.

equipment.label: Pressure sensor (data logger)
equipment.description: Connected to a sealed syringe by a short tube: the gas pressure in kPa, to 0.1 kPa.

equipment.label: Ruler (30 cm)
equipment.description: Held over a tray of water to measure the diameter of a film on its surface.

equipment.label: Ripple tray (30 × 40 cm)
equipment.description: A shallow tray of clean water, its surface dusted with lycopodium powder so that a film spreading on it pushes the powder back into a clear circle.

equipment.label: Ice–salt freezing mixture (about −18 °C)
equipment.description: Crushed ice stirred with a third of its mass of salt in a beaker: a slushy liquid at about −18 °C that takes heat quickly from a tube stood in it.

equipment.label: Simple respirometer (boiling tube, capillary and scale)
equipment.description: A boiling tube sealed by a bung carrying a capillary with a drop of coloured liquid: as the gas inside shrinks or grows the drop moves along the scale, read as the volume of gas to 0.001 mL. Organisms sit on a gauze above soda lime (or none), and a screw clip lets air in to reset it.

equipment.label: Vacuum flask (500 mL), plugged with cotton wool
equipment.description: Double-walled with a vacuum between the walls: heat leaks out about a hundred times more slowly than from an open beaker. The cotton-wool plug lets air in for respiration.

equipment.label: Fly culture vial with food and a foam bung
equipment.description: A tube with a layer of fly food and a foam bung. Kept at 25 °C, a pair of flies leaves its offspring in about ten days; clear the parents after seven so they are not counted with them.

equipment.label: Hand lens and white tile (etherised flies)
equipment.description: Flies knocked out with ether (or carbon dioxide) are tipped onto a white tile, sorted with a fine brush and counted by sex and appearance.

equipment.label: Choice chamber (two-sided)
equipment.description: A shallow dish divided under a gauze floor into two halves: put silica gel (dry) or damp paper (humid) under each half, and cover a half with black card to darken it. Animals go in through the centre of the lid.

equipment.label: Electrode on a crocodile-clip lead
equipment.description: Clip a metal strip or a graphite rod into it (add the electrode as a solid). Unclip the electrode to weigh it: the balance weighs only what the clip holds.

equipment.label: Potometer (bubble potometer, 1 mm capillary)
equipment.description: A water-filled tube with a leafy shoot sealed into one end and a capillary at the other. As the shoot takes up water an air bubble moves along the capillary; its scale reads the volume taken up to 0.001 mL (about 1.3 mm of the capillary). A reservoir resets the bubble.

equipment.label: BOD bottle (300 mL, ground-glass stopper)
equipment.description: Filled to overflowing and stoppered with no bubble, it holds water out of contact with the air, so its dissolved oxygen changes only by what lives in it.

equipment.label: Plant growth cabinet (lit, temperature-controlled)
equipment.description: Fluorescent tubes give about 250 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹; the air is held at a set temperature and about 50 % relative humidity.

equipment.label: Culture tube with cap (glass, 20 mL)
equipment.description: For broths. Flame the neck when it is opened and before it is closed.

equipment.label: Agar deep (narrow tube of set agar)
equipment.description: Stab it with a loaded loop: where growth appears along the stab shows the organism's oxygen requirement.

equipment.label: Agar slope (slant) in a universal
equipment.description: A culture kept on a slope of agar; take cells from it with a loop.

equipment.label: Looking (against the light)
equipment.description: What the eye sees: whether a broth is clear or cloudy, where an agar deep has grown, the colonies on a plate by their look.

equipment.label: Antibiotic susceptibility disc (6 mm)
equipment.description: A paper disc carrying a stated mass of one antibiotic; pressed onto a seeded plate, the drug diffuses out into the agar.

equipment.label: Sterile blank filter-paper disc (13 mm)
equipment.description: A blank paper disc that soaks up about 50 µL: wet it with a test solution, then lay it on a seeded plate.

equipment.label: Zone ruler (millimetres)
equipment.description: Read against a dark background from the back of the plate: the diameter of the clear zone, the disc included, to the nearest millimetre.

equipment.label: UV lamp (long-wave)
equipment.description: Wear UV-protective glasses.

equipment.label: Agarose gel

equipment.label: 4-20 % gradient SDS-polyacrylamide gel, 10 wells (pre-cast)
equipment.description: A gradient gel resolves a wider range than one percentage; its mobility is taken as a 12 % gel's. Stained with Coomassie: a band shows from about 50 ng and stays roughly proportional to a few micrograms.

equipment.label: Size-exclusion column

equipment.label: Analytical size-exclusion column, 10 × 300 mm (1-1300 kDa)
equipment.description: A high-resolution gel-filtration column for a chromatography system: void volume 8 mL, total volume 24 mL, run at 0.5 mL/min.

equipment.label: Desalting column, 8.5 mL bed (excludes above 5 kDa)
equipment.description: Proteins leave in the void volume; salts and small molecules come later.

equipment.label: Pasteur-pipette column of CM-Sephadex G-50 (about 2 mL bed)
equipment.description: A glass Pasteur pipette plugged with glass wool and packed with CM-Sephadex G-50 to 1-1.5 cm from the top. equipment.label: TLC plate, silica gel with F254 indicator (5 × 7 cm, 5 lanes)

equipment.label: UV lamp (long-wave, 365 nm)

equipment.label: UV lamp (short-wave, 254 nm)

equipment.label: Digital thermometer (0.1 °C)

equipment.label: Polystyrene-cup calorimeter with lid
equipment.description: Two nested polystyrene cups with a lid: heat leaks out about 25 times more slowly than from a beaker.

equipment.label: Nickel affinity column, 1 mL bed (His-tag)
equipment.description: Nickel resin holds His-tagged proteins (about 40 mg per mL of bed) until imidazole displaces them; other proteins stick only weakly.

equipment.label: Nitrocellulose membrane in a tray (6 × 8 cm)
equipment.description: Binds any protein that touches it until blocked: block before the antibodies go on.

equipment.label: 6 % native polyacrylamide gel, 10 wells (for gel shifts)
equipment.description: No SDS: proteins keep their shape, so a protein bound to DNA runs with it as a shifted band. Image labelled DNA on a fluorescence imager.

equipment.label: Gel imager (blue-light transilluminator)
equipment.description: Shows stained bands; sizes come from comparison with a ladder.

equipment.label: Fluorescence gel imager
equipment.description: Sees only labelled molecules (a fluorescent probe), about a hundred times more sensitively than a stain, and integrates each band.

equipment.label: 250 mL round-bottom flask (distillation pot)
equipment.description: With anti-bumping granules, a heating mantle, a still head with thermometer and a condenser.

equipment.label: 100 mL round-bottom flask (single neck)
equipment.description: With a stirrer bar: for a reaction heated under reflux, and for taking the solvent off on the rotary evaporator.

equipment.label: 250 mL separating funnel
equipment.description: With a stopper and a tap, in a ring on a stand. Stoppered, it is shaken (venting often) to bring two liquids that do not mix to equilibrium; the layers settle and the lower one runs off through the tap, the stopper out.

equipment.label: Vigreux fractionating column (about 3 theoretical plates)
equipment.description: Fitted between the flask and the still head: the vapour condenses and re-boils on its indentations, a few equilibrium stages in all.

equipment.label: Gel imager (blue-light transilluminator)
equipment.description: Shows where the stained bands are; sizes come from comparison with a ladder.

equipment.label: Sanger sequencing (service)
equipment.description: Reads the DNA in a sample (a PCR product): up to about 1000 bases of the template it mostly holds. Too little DNA gives no readable trace; two templates give double peaks.

equipment.label: Haemocytometer (improved Neubauer) with coverslip
equipment.description: Each large corner square holds 0.1 µL (1 mm × 1 mm × 0.1 mm): cells per square × 10⁴ = cells per mL.

equipment.label: Bench (room temperature)
equipment.description: Open benches: about 0.5 airborne organisms settle per cm² per hour on anything uncovered (a teaching lab in use).

equipment.label: Heating mantle with stirrer and reflux condenser
equipment.description: The flask sits in a heating mantle on a stirrer with a water-cooled condenser in its neck: the mixture boils at its own boiling point and the condensed vapour runs back, so nothing boils away however long it refluxes.

equipment.label: Hot plate
equipment.description: Above 100 °C an aqueous solution boils: it stays at 100 °C and loses solvent.

equipment.label: Lamp (bench lamp with an LED bulb)
equipment.description: What stands in front of it is lit by about 1600 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ at 10 cm, falling as the square of the distance; an LED gives little heat. What it lights stands in a beaker of water (a heat shield) whose temperature can be set. A coloured filter can go in front.

equipment.label: Dark cupboard
equipment.description: No light: for dark controls (or wrap a tube in foil).

equipment.label: Ice–water bath
equipment.description: Ice with water around a flask: cools faster than a bucket of crushed ice.

equipment.label: Thermal cycler, 96 × 0.2 mL tubes (end-point)
equipment.description: Runs a PCR program on tubes; the products are looked at afterwards, on a gel.

equipment.label: Real-time PCR cycler (96-well plate)
equipment.description: Reads every well through the lid after each cycle; its software subtracts each well's baseline and reports the cycle where the signal crosses the threshold (Cq), and can run a melt curve.

equipment.label: Cooled incubator
equipment.description: A refrigerated (BOD) incubator: it holds temperatures below room temperature too.

equipment.description: Long-term storage of enzymes, DNA and finished PCRs.

json.title: Accuracy and precision: a dye standard curve from a weighed stock
json.summary: Weigh about 200 mg of a blue dye powder, make it up to 50.00 mL in a volumetric flask, dilute it to five standards, and measure their absorbance at 628 nm. Then read an unknown three times from fresh portions and report its concentration with the spread of the three.
json.briefing: Accuracy is how close a result is to the true value; precision is how close repeated results are to each other. Neither one implies the other. Zero the spectrophotometer on water, read every solution in the same cuvette type, and keep the standards' range wide enough to bracket the unknown.

json.summary: Set up a compound microscope, see which way round its image is, work up from 4× to 100× oil immersion on a stained blood smear, and compare bright field with phase contrast on living yeast. Then leave it clean.

json.title: Checking micropipettes by weighing
json.summary: Dispense 100 µL of water ten times from each of two P200 pipettes onto an analytical balance, convert each mass to a volume, and work out each pipette's systematic error (accuracy) and coefficient of variation (precision) against the limits for a 200 µL pipette.
json.briefing: Use the semi-micro balance (0.01 mg): at 100 µL a 0.1 mg balance adds about half as much scatter again as the pipette itself. Water's density here is 0.997 g/mL, so 100 µL should weigh 99.7 mg. The mean volume shows a pipette's systematic error; the spread of the ten volumes (as a coefficient of variation) shows its random error. At 100 µL a P200 should be within ±0.8 % systematic and 0.3 % random error. Re-tare before each pipette, and record the cumulative mass after each dispense.

json.title: Micropipettes: choosing, using and proving them
json.summary: Dispense three volumes of water with the pipette suited to each and check them on a balance. Pipette a viscous 50 % glycerol solution forward and in reverse and compare. Then pass a competency test: build exactly 1.000 mL of a four-part mixture in one tube and prove it by weight.
json.briefing: Each micropipette is accurate only within its range, and least accurate near the bottom of it: choose the smallest pipette that holds the volume. Fit a fresh tip, set the volume, press to the first stop before entering the liquid, release slowly, and dispense to the second stop against the tube wall. A viscous liquid lags in the tip and coats it, so forward pipetting delivers short; reverse pipetting (press past the first stop to take up extra, dispense only to the first stop) leaves the excess behind. Water weighs 0.998 g per mL, 50 % (v/v) glycerol 1.130 g per mL.
